summary: Clarify atomic refill and token-slicing interactions for multiplexed orchestrator causing intermittent 429s
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 429s from a dedicated pool while running orchestrated worker fanouts that multiplex many short-lived sessions. The customer suspects token-slicing and atomic refill semantics are causing groups of parallel workers to collide on refill boundaries.

Impact: Roughly 8–12% of requests are receiving 429s during scheduled flush windows for their background ingest and the rate spikes are correlated with their orchestrator job starts. This is causing delays in their pipeline and some time-sensitive webhook retries to fail.

Environment: MetricFlow dedicated pool in prod-us-west, traffic originates from a fleet of orchestrator workers that open ephemeral sessions and use API keys rotated every 6 minutes. Workload pattern: bursts of ~200 short sessions that call streaming start then immediately push small chunks (~1-3k tokens).

Observed behavior: 429s come in tight waves aligned to the orchestrator job start times. Throttle headers show remaining=0 and x-refill-epoch points to a refill event that applied to a group of sessions simultaneously. Customer believes refill is being computed atomically per-namespace and token-sliced windows allow momentary negative bursts.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Create a dedicated pool and provision 2 workers per orchestrator shard.
2) Rotate ephemeral keys every 6 minutes and fanout 200 workers to start within a 30s window.
3) Each worker starts a streaming session and immediately emits a small payload.
4) Observe 429s concentrated within the first 90s of the job.

Request: Customer asks for an explanation of refill semantics when many short-lived sessions start together and guidance on configuration to avoid synchronized 429 waves. They also ask whether splitting refill epochs or changing token-slicing granularity will help and what recommended knob changes are safe for a dedicated pool.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 10:20 UTC - Received initial ticket with customer logs and sample traffic pattern (200 workers, ephemeral keys).

Checked tenant rate limiter logs: refill events recorded at epoch boundaries with batch size consistent with configured burst budget. Noted a cluster of token grants followed by immediate consumption and subsequent remaining=0 for many sessions.
Hypothesis A: Atomic refill per-tenant combined with synchronized session start leads to token allocation granularity causing short-lived sessions to contend and exhaust micro-budgets simultaneously.

Hypothesis B: Token-slicing uses coarse-grain shards (N=8) for this tenant; when many sessions map to same slice the refill appears atomic and causes seen 429 wave. Consider reducing slice size or enabling random jitter on refill mapping.
Observed metric: token_grants_per_epoch spiked from baseline 1200 to 18k during job window; per-slice utilization showed 60% of allocations hitting two slices.
Console trace: route-level latency spiked 5x during event; no 5xxs from serving runtime—rejections are explicit rate rejects.
Customer token rotation pattern (6m TTL) is causing many ephemeral keys to align with refill boundaries due to orchestrator scheduling; recommend reviewing key rotation schedule as well.
Checked linked issue SUP-3141596 for similar refill alignment cases; that ticket implemented refill jitter experiments on staging with positive results.
Action taken so far: increased customer's burst allowance temporarily by +20% for their dedicated pool to provide immediate relief while we evaluate config changes.
Telemetry snapshot saved: s3://redwood-support/telemetry/SUP-527890/epoch-snap-20260312.json (access granted to eng on request).
comments: Priya Agarwal (2026-03-12T11:02Z): Thanks for the report. I've increased a temporary burst buffer on the dedicated pool to reduce immediate impact. Can you send a short window of request IDs and the orchestrator start timestamps so we can correlate?

MetricFlow - Ops (2026-03-12T11:37Z): Provided sample requestIDs and job-start timestamps for two windows (2026-03-11T23:00Z and 2026-03-12T03:00Z). Noted pattern: starts are scheduled by cron jobs in their orchestrator which align closely with system clocks across shards.

Ethan Chen (SRE) (2026-03-12T13:10Z): Observed per-slice hot-spotting. Tentative plan: run a controlled experiment to change slice_count from 8 to 32 for this tenant in staging and add random refill jitter of up to 30s to epoch boundary. Asking Product if jitter change is safe for SLA window accounting.

Product (2026-03-12T14:05Z): Jitter change acceptable at customer-level for non-critical low-latency lanes. For higher tiers would need rollout notes. Suggest start with orchestrator/background lane only.

MetricFlow - Dev (2026-03-12T15:22Z): We can stagger cron starts by introducing per-shard random delay up to 45s. But we'd prefer config guidance on the server side so we don't have to change many orchestrators across fleets.

Ethan Chen (2026-03-13T09:40Z): Deployed slice_count=32 and refill_jitter=20s in staging for a shadow of MetricFlow traffic. Early results: reduction in 429 wave amplitude by ~70% in staging shadow runs. Preparing rollout playbook.

Priya Agarwal (2026-03-14T08:12Z): Noted that customer agreed to a staged rollout: apply slice_count increase + refill jitter to background-lane only, monitor for billing/console effects, then decide on global lane changes. Will coordinate maintenance window.
MetricFlow - Ops (2026-03-14T12:01Z): Thank you, please proceed with background-lane change during our maintenance window 2026-03-15 02:00-03:00 UTC. We'll monitor.
resolution: Temporary burst allowance increased +20%; staging experiment with slice_count=32 and refill_jitter=20s reduced 429 wave amplitude by ~70%. Planned staged rollout to customer background lane during maintenance window. Final resolution pending production rollout and 48h monitoring.
